sphere_refinement.doc:
Type: list({'edge_size':float, 'radius':float, 'center':[float, float, float]}) 
   Default: []                                                            
   
   Specify a list of edge size, radius and center for spheres used for    
   sphere refinement meshing. This is used to create different mesh       
   densities for different regions of the solid model based on sphere     
   geometry.                                                              
   
   The 'edge_size' parameter is the maxium length of an element edge for  
   the nodes within a sphere.                                             
   
   The 'radius' parameter is the radius of a sphere.                      
   
   The 'center' parameter is the center of a sphere.                      
   
   Sphere refinement values are not checked when the values are set.      
   Errors in the values (e.g. a misspelled dict key) are not reported     
   until they used for generating a mesh.                                 
   
   Using sphere refinemen for meshing is enabled by setting the           
   'sphere_refinement_on' meshing option to True.                         
   
   Example: Setting values for the sphere refinement option               
   
      options.sphere_refinement.append( {'edge_size':0.2, 'radius':3.7,  
         'center':[1.4, -1.0, 0.078] })                                  
      options.sphere_refinement_on = True

sphere_refinement_on.doc:
Type: bool                                                             
   Default: False                                                         
   
   If True then enable sphere refinement meshing.

radius_meshing_centerlines.doc:
Type: vtkPolyData object                                                
   Default: None                                                           
   
   The vtkPolyData object used to store centerline geometry for radius-based 
   meshing. The centerline geometry read in or computed can be stored in   
   is parameter so it can be reused when changing other meshing options.   
   
   If 'radius_meshing_centerlines' is not set then centerline geometry is  
   computed for the current solid model. The 'radius_meshing_centerlines'  
   is then set with the computed centerlines.                              
   
   Example: Reading in centerlines and saving them in options              
   
      centerlines_file = "centerlines.vtp"                               
      reader = vtk.vtkXMLPolyDataReader()                                  
      reader.SetFileName(centerlines_file)                                 
      reader.Update()                                                      
      options.radius_meshing_centerlines = reader.GetOutput()

quality_ratio.doc:
Type: float                                                             
   Default: 1.4                                                            
   
   The quality measure for the mesh. This number corresponds to the ratio  
   between the radius of the circumsphere of an element and the maximum    
   edge size.

Type: bool

   If True then generate a volume mesh.

no_bisect.doc:
Type: bool                                                              
   Default: True                                                           
   If True then use the solid model surface mesh for the volume mesh.

minimum_dihedral_angle.doc:
Type: float                                                             
   Default: 0.0                                                            
   
   The minimum allowable dihedral angle for an element in the mesh. The    
   dihedral is the angle between two adjacent faces for an element.

radius_meshing_scale.doc:
Type: float                                                             
   Default: 0.1                                                            
   
   The scale value determines the mesh size factor used to set a variable  
   edge size for meshing based on the distance of solid model surface nodes 
   to centerline geometry.                                                 
   
   The mesh size factor is calculated for each surface node using          
   
       size_factor = scale * (distance to centerline) / min_dist           
   
   where min_dist is the minumum node to centerline distance.

optimization.doc:
Type: int                                                               
   Default: 3                                                              
   
   The number of times to optimize the mesh. Optimization moves nodes to   
   obtain a better quality mesh.

local_edge_size.doc:
Type: list({'face_id':int, 'edge_size':float})                         
   Default: []                                                            
   
   Specify a list of local edge sizes for solid model faces. This is used 
   to create different mesh densities for different regions of the solid  
   model.                                                                 
   
   The 'face_id' parameter is an integer ID identifying a solid model     
   face. The solid model face IDs are obtained using the TetGen mesher    
   get_model_face_ids() method.                                           
   
   The 'edge_size' parameter is the maxium length of an element edge for  
   the face.                                                              
   
   Edge size values are not checked when the values are set. Errors in    
   the values (e.g. a misspelled dict key) are not reported until they    
   used for generating a mesh.                                            
   
   Using local edge sizes for meshing is enabled by setting the           
   'local_edge_size_on' meshing option to True.                           
   
   Example: Setting values for the local edge sizes option                
   
      options.local_edge_size = [ {'face_id':1, 'edge_size':0.3} ]        
      options.local_edge_size_on = True

meshing_module_doc:
SimVascular meshing module. 
   
   The meshing module provides an interface to SV meshing functionality    
   used to generate a finite element tetrahedral mesh from a solid model.  
   
   Methods are provided for setting meshing parameters, generating meshes  
   and extracting mesh results as VTK unstructured mesh objects.           
   
   Two mesh generation software components are supported:                  
       (1) TetGen  
       (2) MeshSim 
   
   TetGen is an open source software package used to generate meshes from  
   PolyData solid models.                                                  
   
   MeshSim is a commercial software package used to generate meshes from   
   Parasolid solid models. Using MeshSim requires purchasing a license from
   Simmetrix, a Parasolid license from Siemens and SV plugins providing an 
   an interface to the software.                                           
   
   Meshing kernels are identified using the meshing.Kernel class:           
       (1) Kernel.TETGEN                                                    
       (2) Kernel.MESHSIM

TetGenOptions(global_edge_size=None, surface_mesh_flag=None,            
                 volume_mesh_flag=None)                                     
   
   The TetGenOptions class stores parameter values used to control how      
   TetGen generates a finite element mesh.                                  
   
   Example: Create a TetGen options object with default parameter values

        edge.                                                               
     surface_mesh_flag (Optional[bool]): If True then perform surface       
         remeshing.                                                         
     volume_mesh_flag (Optional[bool]): If True then generate a volume mesh.

methods.compute_model_boundary_faces:
compute_model_boundary_faces(angle)  
   
   Compute the boundary faces for the solid model. 
   
   This method needs to be called only for PolyData solid models that do    
   not have face information already defined (e.g. models from STL files).  
   It does not need to be called for OpenCascade or Parasolid models.       
   
   For PolyData models faces are distinguished using the angle of the       
   normals between adjacent triangles. If the angle is less than or equal   
   to the 'angle' argument then the triangles are considered to part of     
   the same face. 
   
   Args:                                    
     angle (double): The angle in degrees used to determine the boundary faces of the solid model.
